summary: Susanne Mrozik works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an M.T.S. at Harvard University, studying with Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, Margaret R. Miles, and doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey. She held posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

Sushanta Sen worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. After studying at Visva-Bharati University, he served there as a lecturer in 1986, and later as a Lecturer in Indian Religions at the University of Birmingham.

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1992–2001) under Makio Takemura. He held part-time lecturer posts at Kyoto University (~2008), Hanazono University (~2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (~2012–2013).
Susumu Sakurabe is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University from circa 1945 to 1950 and later served there as a professor from circa 1968 to 1991.

Susumu Shimazono is a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1977). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1982–1987), University of Tokyo (~1987–2013), and Sophia University (~2013–2021), and served as president of the Japanese Association for Religious Studies (~2002–2005).

Susumu Yamaguchi specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani and Kyoto universities under Gessho Sasaki, Enga Teramoto, Sylvain Lévi, and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as a professor at Otani University and Kyoto Sangyo University.
Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College. He held posts at the University of Toronto (~1986–2006) and Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001).

Suzanne Karpelès worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1917 to 1922 and held a post at the French Information Bureau from circa 1945 to 1949.

Suzanne Newcombe works in religious studies and Indology. After earning a doctorate at the University of Cambridge (attested 2008), she held posts at Cambridge, LSE, Inform (attested 2008, 2020), King's College London (attested 2020), and the Open University (attested 2020).
Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Syed Ali Bilgrami worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Lucknow, IIT Roorkee (~1873–1876), and the University of London (~1876–1879), before serving in the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and as Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (~1902–1911).

Syed Hasan Askari was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College (~1918–1922), and Patna University (~1922–1925), and later served as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).
Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar of history and archaeology. Attested in 1932, he served as Professor of Persian at Baroda College and as Principal of Bahauddin College.
Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1980 and held a post at Aix-Marseille University.

Sylvain Lévi specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Lycée Charlemagne and EPHE, he held chairs at the University of Paris, EPHE, Collège de France, and Maison Franco-Japonaise.

Sze-bong Tso specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.
Søren Sørensen was an Indology scholar who held posts at Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1887 to 1902.

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indology scholar who studied as a pupil under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at The Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), succeeding T. R. Chintamani.

T. Griffith Foulk is a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1978–1987) under Luis Oscar Gómez, later teaching there (~1987–1995) and at Sarah Lawrence College (~1995–2012).

T. R. Chintamani was an Indology scholar who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Manager and Correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras (~1927) and as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (attested 1938–1951).
